source_checks.title: Hawaii DLNR Division of Forestry and Wildlife
CIFFC National Fire Situation Report
source_checks.detail: Machine collector received a minimal response; browser review rendered the Aug 7 situation report and the Aug 8 current-fires summary, with the situation page one publication cycle behind the execution date.

national_posture.statement: The August 7 IMSR placed the United States at National Preparedness Level 5, with 95 uncontained large fires, 140 active incidents, and 30,132 personnel assigned.
national_posture.level_meaning: national resources are fully committed, active geographic areas may need emergency measures, and potential for additional significant fires is high

national_posture.statement: The latest CIFFC situation report available at the cutoff, updated August 7, kept Canada at National Preparedness Level 5. The Aug 8 CIFFC current-fires summary showed 123 full-response fires covering 988,546.8 hectares and 4,566 fires covering 3,902,318.5 hectares year to date.
national_posture.level_meaning: national demand is extreme, resources are fully committed, and international resources are being mobilized to sustain operations

incidents.name: Old Trails Fire
incidents.location: West of Spokane near Airway Heights
incidents.controlling_agency: California Interagency Incident Management Team 7 and Washington Department of Natural Resources

evacuation.description: Evacuations and area, road, and trail closures remained in effect around the Spokane fires.

incidents.operational_outlook: The Aug 8 incident information reports continued structure protection, perimeter control, and mop-up; the Aug 7 IMSR described moderate fire behavior.

attention.coverage_summary: Coverage focused on the arson case, extensive structure loss, evacuee recovery, assistance for affected residents, and containment progress.
attention.methodology_note: Browser-visible search was capped at 100 unique result links; counts are censored observations and no auditable public-discussion count was available.

incidents.analyst_note: **Cat-modeling interpretation:** The IMSR's 600 losses are unspecified structures and must not be converted into dwellings. ([NIFC IMSR](https://www.nifc.gov/nicc/sitreprt.pdf))
critical_alert_reasons: at least 25 newly damaged or destroyed structures
named community under evacuation with structure involvement or imminent threat

incidents.name: Widemouth 2 Fire
incidents.location: Fishlake National Forest between Kanosh, Meadow, and Fillmore
incidents.controlling_agency: Great Basin Complex Incident Management Team 2 and Fishlake National Forest

evacuation.description: The IMSR reported evacuations, road and area closures; the incident page directs residents to local evacuation information.

incidents.operational_outlook: The August 7 IMSR reported extreme fire behavior and numerous structures and infrastructure threatened.

attention.coverage_summary: Coverage was dominated by the crash of a firefighting helicopter assigned to the incident, uncertainty over the two people aboard at the cutoff, continued fire growth, closures, and difficult containment conditions.
attention.methodology_note: The browser-visible sample met the High threshold; news-area estimates do not replace the official IMSR acreage, and no fatality is recorded because officials had not confirmed the occupants' status at the cutoff.

incidents.analyst_note: **Source reconciliation:** The direct incident page was stale at cutoff; the newer August 7 IMSR controls the 99,485-acre, 19%-contained operational record. ([NIFC IMSR](https://www.nifc.gov/nicc/sitreprt.pdf))
critical_alert_reasons: named community under evacuation with structure involvement or imminent threat

incidents.name: Grasshopper Fire
incidents.location: Mt. Hood National Forest near Highway 35
incidents.controlling_agency: U.S. Forest Service, Mt. Hood National Forest

evacuation.description: Incident information directs residents to current county evacuation levels and notes a forest closure order.

incidents.operational_outlook: The incident page retained evacuation guidance and closures; the IMSR reported active behavior with structures and critical infrastructure threatened.

attention.coverage_summary: Coverage emphasized growth, Highway 35 closures, evacuation constraints, Mount Hood access, National Guard support, and power-protection measures.
attention.methodology_note: Result count is a browser-visible, title-attributed sample; no auditable public-discussion count was available.

incidents.analyst_note: **Cat-modeling interpretation:** Official sources report qualitative structural and infrastructure threat, not a numeric structure-loss count. ([InciWeb](https://inciweb.wildfire.gov/incident-information/ormhf-grasshopper))
critical_alert_reasons: named community under evacuation with structure involvement or imminent threat

incidents.name: Wrights Spring Fire
incidents.location: Southeast of Chiloquin in Klamath County
incidents.controlling_agency: Northwest Complex Incident Management Team 8 and Oregon State Fire Marshal Green Incident Management Team

evacuation.description: Level 1, 2, and 3 evacuations were in effect for Sprague River and along Sprague River Road east of Chiloquin, with a Red Cross shelter at Chiloquin Elementary School.

incidents.operational_outlook: The incident team reported extreme fire behavior that temporarily forced crews to withdraw, ordered additional resources, and assigned dozers and Oregon State Fire Marshal crews to overnight structure protection.

attention.coverage_summary: Coverage centered on the official fire-line fatality, rapid growth, escalating Level 3 evacuations, the Emergency Conflagration Act response, and structure-protection operations.
attention.methodology_note: The 24-hour sample remained below the 40-item High threshold; the seven-day baseline was estimated from 43 visible results divided by seven, and no auditable public-discussion count was available.

incidents.analyst_note: **Cat-modeling interpretation:** No structure-loss count was reported, but the confirmed fire-line fatality, named-community evacuation orders, extreme behavior, and overnight structure protection make this a critical catastrophe-intelligence event. ([Klamath County Sheriff's Office fatality statement](https://www.facebook.com/KlamathSheriff/posts/a-tragic-lossthe-wrights-spring-fire-has-claimed-the-life-of-jason-ensign-a-47-y/1031417396144922/); [Wrights Spring Fire evening update](https://www.facebook.com/SCOFMPFIREINFO/posts/evening-update-8726wrights-spring-fire-current-situation-the-northwest-complex-i/1482690113895193/))
critical_alert_reasons: named community under evacuation with structure involvement or imminent threat

incidents.name: Aspen Acres Fire
incidents.controlling_agency: Rocky Mountain Complex Incident Management Team 3

evacuation.description: Area and road closures remained in effect; the reviewed update did not quantify active evacuations.

incidents.operational_outlook: Minimal fire behavior continued at 72% containment, while managers warned that a warming and drying trend could increase activity over the next several days.

attention.coverage_summary: Coverage emphasized stable containment near 71%, road reopening, the handoff to a smaller management team, and community recovery rather than a new loss increment.
attention.methodology_note: No auditable public-discussion count was available.

incidents.analyst_note: **Cat-modeling interpretation:** The 915 lost structures are cumulative and unspecified by occupancy. ([NIFC IMSR](https://www.nifc.gov/nicc/sitreprt.pdf))

incidents.name: Bradley Creek Fire
incidents.location: Okanagan Indian Band reserve near Vernon

evacuation.description: Evacuation orders and alerts remained mapped around the Okanagan Indian Band and neighboring jurisdictions.

incidents.operational_outlook: CIFFC retained Bradley Creek as an out-of-control priority fire; current coverage described smoke moderating behavior but wind risk ahead.

attention.coverage_summary: Coverage centered on the Okanagan Indian Band's recovery, smoke effects on behavior, evacuation changes, utility risk, and strengthening winds.
attention.methodology_note: No auditable public-discussion count was available.

incidents.analyst_note: **Cat-modeling interpretation:** The roughly 230-home estimate is preliminary and is not a completed parcel-level assessment. ([Associated Press](https://apnews.com/article/wildfire-canada-homes-destroyed-british-columbia-fbbb7f027adb04a9c9b47a109de74082))
critical_alert_reasons: at least 25 newly damaged or destroyed structures

incidents.name: Pear Lake Fire
incidents.location: Thompson-Nicola Regional District and Village of Clinton

evacuation.description: Evacuation orders and alerts remained mapped across regional districts, First Nations, and the Village of Clinton.

incidents.operational_outlook: CIFFC retained Pear Lake as an out-of-control priority fire; current coverage warned of potential aggressive behavior and further growth.

attention.coverage_summary: Coverage focused on additional evacuation orders, smoke effects, readiness for rapid evacuation, and the potential for aggressive behavior and growth.
attention.methodology_note: No auditable public-discussion count was available.

incidents.analyst_note: **Cat-modeling interpretation:** Do not equate about 120 affected properties with destroyed dwellings; reported impacts include non-residential structures and assessment remained incomplete. ([CTV News](https://www.ctvnews.ca/vancouver/article/more-than-100-structures-lost-in-bcs-pear-lake-wildfire-officials-say/))

global_overview.statement: The reviewed 24-hour international headline sample was concentrated in Europe's heat-driven wildfire activity, led by reported home destruction northwest of Athens, settlement-adjacent fires in Serbia, and a new fire near Narbonne, France. This is a headline scan, not comprehensive worldwide operational intelligence.

global_events.name: Western Attica wildfire
global_events.status: Current coverage showed a fast-moving wildfire northwest of Athens burning through homes, farmland, and animal habitat while crews continued containment work
global_events.structure_loss_description: More than 100 homes were reported destroyed in the reviewed headline source; this was not independently reconciled to a controlling Greek operational update.
global_events.summary: The event was promoted for reported structural loss, but the available English-language sample did not provide a defensible ignition date or consolidated operational perimeter.

global_events.name: Deliblato Sands and Serbia wildfires
global_events.status: Helicopters and ground crews fought a major fire in the Deliblato Sands reserve while eight other fires affected parts of Serbia during extreme heat and drought
global_events.evacuations: Residents of Sumarak were asked to leave as a precaution; the reviewed Associated Press report said no houses had burned and no casualties were reported.
global_events.summary: The army joined the response, and officials described the nationwide situation as serious but not critical.

global_events.name: Narbonne-area wildfire
global_events.status: Water-bombing aircraft and helicopters fought a wildfire in the Corbières massif near Narbonne after a road accident
global_events.summary: The reviewed headline source reported no consolidated structural-loss or casualty figure.
